project.title: FleetCentric research
project.subtitle: Route optimization and rerouting for FAST NUCES Karachi shuttles
project.question: Can good shuttle routes be planned, and re-planned when a road is blocked, within free-tier compute limits (512 MB RAM, 0.1 CPU)?
caveats: Students are synthetic (bus loads 65 to 90 percent of capacity), not real registrations.
Travel times are free-flow OSRM times with no traffic; real morning times are higher.
Rerouting scope for FYP-1: morning runs to campus only, one bus rerouted at a time.
Traffic-aware planning with uneven, time-of-day travel times is deferred to FYP-2; the traffic check scaled every road equally.
Rerouting truth is OSRM, which picks routes by its internal weight, not by time: 0.30% of travel times get slightly faster after a closure. Every method is scored on the same table.

items.title: Optimization
items.question: Can all-stop routes be built from a travel-time matrix within free-tier CPU and memory limits, and how do they compare with the current hand-made routes?

items.title: Rerouting
items.question: When a road is blocked, which road and which stops (keep, skip, or let students walk to a nearby point) give the lowest student delay, within the same limits?

items.title: Context
items.question: How much do real incidents slow shuttle routes, recorded on an H3 grid?

items.title: Prediction
items.question: Does that context predict travel times better than the timetable and the router?

Internal review of both chapters by a second person (by Fri 4 Dec); then the hub plan, the progress tracker and the shared page brought up to date (by Sun 6 Dec).

experiments.title: Time-budget experiment
experiments.question: On a free-tier server (512 MB, no swap, 0.1 CPU), how close does the optimizer get to the best known plan, and how fast?
experiments.design: Each contractor solved at 10, 60, 300 and 600 s, 3 repeats, limited and unlimited, plus one 30-minute unlimited reference. 50 runs, about 4.5 hours. Limits applied with systemd cgroups in WSL.

experiments.title: Query-budget experiment
experiments.question: How few real travel-time queries (each stop's K nearest stops plus its leg to campus, the rest estimated) still give routes within 3% of the full matrix?
experiments.design: K = 0, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40 with two estimators (straight-line fit, shortest path through queried legs) plus the full matrix as control; 2 contractors, 3 repeats, 60 s unlimited search. Plans are scored on real OSRM times. 72 runs, about 40 minutes on 2 cores.

experiments.title: Traffic check

experiments.title: Optimizer scaling (Windows laptop)
experiments.question: How do the optimizer's build time, memory and plan quality grow as stops and buses grow, and does handing OR-Tools the travel times as a matrix instead of a Python callback change that?
experiments.design: Instances Jadoon (171 stops), Nadeem (143), All (311, both fleets), All-doubled (622), and Jadoon-doubled (342) and Nadeem-doubled (286); a doubled instance copies every stop 30 s from its original and every bus, so it tests model size, not geography. Lookups callback and matrix; 300 s each, no limits, each run a fresh process: 12 runs, about an hour. No pass/fail threshold: it reports curves. All and All-doubled need the combined matrix (OSRM) and are recorded as skipped without it; the doubled contractor instances stand in for size until then. Peak memory is the OS's figure for the machine that ran it (Linux ru_maxrss, Windows peak working set). All and All-doubled ran on the Docker laptop on 19 Nov, once the combined matrix existed, and are in their own entry (Optimizer scaling, WSL); the 'skipped' rows for them here are from 17 Nov. Rows from the two machines are never pooled, so this entry runs the four contractor instances only.

experiments.question: How do the optimizer's build time, memory and plan quality grow as stops and buses grow, and does handing OR-Tools the travel times as a matrix instead of a Python callback change that?
experiments.design: All (311 stops, 53 buses, both fleets) and All-doubled (622, 106) on the Docker laptop in WSL, 19 Nov, code 975760c: both lookups, 300 s each, no limits, each run a fresh process. Needs the combined matrix (data/matrix_fall2026_v1_all.json). Run OS1 is these 4 runs plus the 8 of 'Optimizer scaling (Windows laptop)'; the two machines' rows are not pooled.

experiments.title: Optimizer scaling (WSL, all six instances, one machine)
experiments.question: How do the optimizer's build time, memory and plan quality grow as stops and buses grow, and does handing OR-Tools the travel times as a matrix instead of a Python callback change that?
experiments.design: Run OS1 repeated on one machine (the Docker laptop, WSL), 20 Nov, so all six instances share one machine, one code version and one meta file: Jadoon (171 stops), Nadeem (143), Jadoon-doubled (342), Nadeem-doubled (286), All (311) and All-doubled (622); both lookups, 300 s each, no limits, each run a fresh process: 12 runs, about an hour. Optimizer code unchanged since 975760c; code a7f3fe2, 12 of 12 ok (L11). The four contractor runs were repeated after a fix to where run_scale.py writes the per-run file (relative --out-dir). Supersedes the two-machine split for the chapter's curves; the earlier entries stay as recorded.

experiments.title: Rerouting quality pass
experiments.question: When a road on a bus's route is closed, how much does letting students walk to another stop gain over the patched published route, beyond what skipping a stop saves on a normal day, and is the fast greedy method close to the exact one?
experiments.design: Every frozen scenario (about 210: two 200 m full-block closures per route, two bus positions each, plus the historical Shahrah-e-Faisal block and University Road ponding, reported apart) x walking limits 0, 400 and 800 m x R0 (patched route), R2 (greedy, then improvement rounds) and R3 (exact) on true OSRM times with no time limit. At 400 m two more arms: the no-closure control (same solve on unblocked times) and must-serve (25% of stops, fixed draw). Judged on synthetic scenarios with at least 2 remaining stops where R0 loses at least 60 s: median closure-specific gain at least 60 s; R2 within 60 s of R3 in 90% of scenarios and on every route's median; no failed run. runs_total is set by the script from the scenario file (5 rows per scenario).

chips.label: Walking gains at least 60 s net of the no-closure control (400 m, median)
Greedy within 60 s of the exact plan in 90% of scenarios and on every route's median (400 m)
No failed run, no avoidable unserved stop, exact never later than the patched route

per_route.worst_by: median R2 minus R3 delay at 400 m

experiments.title: Rerouting limits pass
experiments.question: On a free-tier server (512 MB, no swap, 0.1 CPU), with the road graph already loaded, how fast does the rerouter have a valid plan, and how close to the oracle is it at 30 s?
experiments.design: Every scenario at 400 m. One worker process per route, arm and repeat loads the graph once and solves that route's scenarios in turn. Arms: plan on the road graph under the limits with a 30 s cap (3 repeats, judged); plan on the graph with no limits (graph error alone); plan on true times under the limits (time limit alone). Every plan is scored on true times against the oracle (R3 on true times, no limit). Judged on the worst repeat: a valid plan within 5 s in 95% of judged scenarios; within 60 s of the oracle at 30 s in 90%; peak memory under 400 MB including the graph. Limits applied with systemd cgroups in WSL; runs_total is set by the script (7 rows per scenario).

At 30 s within 60 s of the oracle in 90% of scenarios (graph, limited, worst repeat)

experiments.title: Rerouting scaling (Windows laptop, stops, no limits)
experiments.question: How do decision time and memory grow with stops on one bus, with the size of the road graph searched, and with the number of buses one closure hits at once, and what does solving in slices cost?
experiments.design: Stops: synthetic problems with 4 to 20 remaining stops and 1, 2 or 4 extra boarding points per stop, 3 seeds, limited and unlimited (R3 not run above 16 stops; a lower bound instead). Graph: 10, 30 and 60 points on the longest route's corridor and on the whole city, limited and unlimited. Buses: the Shahrah-e-Faisal closure hitting 1, 5, 10 and 20 buses in one limited process sharing the row cache. Slices: the three largest judged scenarios solved 256 masks at a time, with plan quality and saved-state size after each slice. Each measurement runs in a fresh process. No pass/fail threshold: it reports curves. On 20 Nov every part (stops limited and unlimited, graph, buses, slices) ran in WSL with systemd into results/reroute-scale-wsl/ (its own entry). This entry keeps the 17 Nov Windows rows (stops, no limits) and runs only those; the two machines' rows are never pooled.

thresholds.note: curves only, no pass or fail
